prompt: Finance counted 11,239 order lines for store BE-14 in 2024. Does the data agree once resent copies are removed? These tables may hold errors. Two lines are copies of one order line when order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id and line_discount_eur all match, with a missing promo_id matching a missing one; keep one line of each such set. 2024 means order_ts, as stored, from 1 January 2024 up to but not including 1 January 2025. Return three columns, in this order: n_stored, the lines as stored, n_unique, the lines with copies removed, and result: 'pass' when n_unique is 11,239, otherwise 'fail'. The result is a single row. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the result column that compares the copy-free count with finance's figure.
Each group of matching lines is one real line, so the number of groups is the copy-free count; a CASE turns the comparison into pass or fail.
faded_shape:
WITH be14_lines AS (  -- one row per BE-14 order line of 2024, as stored
  SELECT ol.order_id, ol.product_id, ol.quantity, ol.unit_price_eur, ol.promo_id, ol.line_discount_eur
  FROM order_lines ol
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
  JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
  WHERE s.store_code = 'BE-14'
    AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01'
),
line_sets AS (  -- one row per set of matching lines
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_lines
  FROM be14_lines
  GROUP BY order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price_eur, promo_id, line_discount_eur
)
SELECT SUM(n_lines) AS n_stored, COUNT(*) AS n_unique,
why_this_works: Each set of matching lines counts once, so the number of sets is the copy-free count that finance's figure should match.
